J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "The set of edges C_ij connecting a component of G[S] to a component of G[T] is a cut-set." The first-choice line 36 is "Claim: Cij is a cut-set", where line 24 defines "Cij = {e in C : e connects a vertex in Si to a vertex in Tj}", line 18 and line 20 make Si and Tj the components of G[S] and G[T], and line 5-7 (Definition 1) fix "cut-set" as delta(S') = E(S',T') for a partition V = S' u T' with both parts non-empty. So the line asserts precisely the challenged proposition, under exactly those assumptions; line 35 announces it as part of proving "Cij = delta(Si) is a bond".

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A concrete small graph with the partition, the components and the resulting edge set: "In a 4-cycle v1-v2-v3-v4-v1 with S={v1,v3} and T={v2,v4}, the set of edges between S_1={v1} and T_1={v2} is exactly the single edge (v1,v2), which is not a cut-set." Every object the claim mentions is instantiated.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exhaustive enumeration of exactly the supplied instance (script kept). In the 4-cycle, V = {v1,v3} u {v2,v4} is a partition with both parts non-empty, so it is an instance of the source's setup; C = delta(S) is all four edges; G[S] has components {v1} and {v3} and G[T] has components {v2} and {v4}, so S_1 = {v1} and T_1 = {v2} as the response says, and C_11 = {(v1,v2)}, a single edge. Enumerating delta(S') over all 14 non-trivial partitions of the four vertices gives exactly seven cut-sets, all of even size (six of size 2 and one of size 4); the singleton {(v1,v2)} is not among them, so it is not a cut-set in the sense of Definition 1. Deleting it also leaves the graph connected (one component before and after), so it is not a minimal cut under the alternative wording of Definition 2 at lines 10-11 either. The supplied witness therefore satisfies the source's assumptions and refutes line 36 as written.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response lists three candidate lines (0036, 0034, 0060), a claim and a counterexample, and states no consequence. In particular it does not assert that Theorem 1 at lines 12-13 is false - which would have been an overreach, since the theorem is a standard true statement and what fails is this proof's component-pair decomposition - and it makes no claim about the remark at lines 62-64.

notes: Clean and decisive: in the witness the cut C is the whole 4-cycle's edge set and every C_ij is a single edge, while every cut-set of a cycle has even size, so none of the four pieces is a cut-set and the decomposition of Step 2 cannot be into bonds. For the second reader: the source's own Step 3 hedges ("However, we need to show Cij itself is a cut-set", line 44, and "we claim that Cij = delta(Tj) cap delta(Si) when both sets are considered within the context of the original cut", lines 49-50), so line 36 is asserted and then never established, which is consistent with the response's diagnosis.
